text.p: English champions Manchester United gave a huge boost to their squad for next season on Friday by signing England striker Teddy Sheringham from Tottenham Hotspur.

Sheringham, who had requested a transfer from Spurs because he was unhappy that the club was not challenging for major honours, joined the European Cup semifinalists for a fee in the region of 3.5 million pounds sterling ($5.8 million).

The 31-year-old forward, who has enjoyed a successful partnership with Alan Shearer in the national team, is United's biggest close-season signing. The transfer came as a huge surprise to the English game.
There had been speculation that Sheringham might move abroad to Italy but he has taken the opportunity to join Britain's most prestigious club as he moves into the later part of his career.
"There are two or three reasons for the decision. But basically I came to the decision that I would like a fresh challenge," he told reporters.
"They are expected to win things and I like the sound of that. You are in football to win things and it is about time I did...I'm elated. It all came out of the blue."
United now have a quality attacking player to replace Frenchman Eric Cantona who recently announced his retirement from the game.
Sheringham said the deal was struck very quickly after he returned from holiday this week. He said he was not worried about stepping into Cantona's shoes.
"People are going to make comparisons but I can only do what I am good at," he said.

Sheringham had been at Tottenham since 1992. Ironically his first match for United could be against the London club at White Hart Lane on August 10 on the opening weekend of the premier league season.
"What a fixture that is," Sheringham said. "There is going to be a lot of hype but I have to look at it as another game."
Spurs were originally believed to have asked six million pounds ($10 million) for Sheringham but United were said to have been wary of paying that much for a player over 30.
